report:
Reviewed the complete canonical_cycles claim, its sole implementation association, and its complete associated test set. Requirements are: recursive answers depend on canonical cycles rather than polling order; repeated canonical goals distinguish inductive, coinductive, and unknown paths; provisional answers are evaluated to a fixpoint; and infinitely growing distinct goals produce overflow under deterministic structural limits rather than being mistaken for a repeated cycle. The only implementation entry is explicitly TODO in sage_meta::todo in semantic_spec.rs. Its explanation states that the existing provisional inductive cutoff and depth limit do not implement path-kind-aware canonical-cycle fixpoints. This is an adequate explicit deferral of the central canonical-cycle machinery, not ordinary implementation evidence. In particular it does not assert that the depth limit proves deterministic structural overflow or that a cutoff supplies coinductive/unknown semantics.
The sole associated test, sage_meta::todo::solver_canonical_cycles, is an empty explicitly TODO test. It has no behavioral assertions and establishes none of the requirements. Its comment explicitly specifies future recursive clause families for inductive failure, coinductive success, unknown-path ambiguity, converging and non-converging fixpoints, non-repeating growth overflow, and ready-queue perturbation invariance. Together these cover every required distinction, including the boundary between repeated canonical goals and unbounded distinct goals. The prerequisite is the path-kind-aware provisional canonical-cycle/fixpoint implementation and deterministic structural resource accounting identified as absent by the implementation TODO; the future queue perturbation fixture must be able to drive the same goal graph in different polling orders. The placeholder must remain deferred until these fixtures contain real assertions against that machinery. No N/A or ordinary implemented/tested entries are present, and no assertion or passing placeholder is credited as behavioral coverage.
Accepted the existing explicit implementation and test deferrals; this review does not certify the claimed functionality as implemented. Source inspection and review start/read/record are the only work performed for this anchor; no behavioral tests were executed and no Rust or specification edits were made. Captured the review-policy dependency with review read. No additional source helper dependency is needed for assessing this wholly deferred association and its visible empty test body.
